product_overview: IMS is an Arabic-first assessment platform for creating exams, managing candidates, assigning secure exam links, delivering timed sittings, and reviewing or marking results. It supports staff workflows for authoring, administration, monitoring, and reporting, while candidates take exams directly from invitation links without creating accounts.
core_goals: Create and publish exams with questions, sections, and reusable blueprint structures
Manage candidates, groups, and exam assignments with secure per-recipient links
Allow candidates to open an invitation link, start an exam, answer questions, and submit within a timed session
Support staff review and marking for answers that require manual grading
Provide results dashboards and candidate result views after scoring is complete
Configure organisation branding, defaults, and access settings
Administer staff users, roles, and multi-organisation deployment where applicable

features.name: Sitting an exam from a link
features.description: A candidate opens a secure invitation link, reviews the exam details, starts the sitting, answers within a server-controlled timer, submits, and then sees the released outcome or a withheld-results message.
user_flows: Navigate to /exam/:token -> Read the exam title, duration, and attempts left -> Start the exam -> Answer questions -> Move between questions using the question map -> Watch the remaining time count down -> Submit the exam -> See the result or a withheld-results message

features.name: Answering supported question types
features.description: A candidate responds to the question using the control matched to that question type, and the answer is saved while they continue working.
user_flows: Navigate to /exam/:token/sitting -> Choose one option or several options -> Type a written answer, number, or code -> Drag or reorder items -> Pair items across two columns -> Point at a place on an image -> Upload a file or record audio

features.name: Signing in as staff
features.description: Staff members sign in with their account credentials and return to the application with access limited by their role.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Enter username -> Enter password -> Sign in -> Return to the app and see the pages allowed by the assigned role

features.name: Authoring an exam and its questions
features.description: A staff author creates an exam, adds questions, imports questions from CSV, defines blueprint rules, and publishes the exam once it is ready.
user_flows: Navigate to /exams -> Create a new exam -> Enter a title, duration, and pass mark -> Save the exam -> Add questions by choosing a type and filling the editor -> Import questions from CSV and review the preview -> Open the blueprint view -> Add sections and draw rules from the shared bank -> Publish the exam -> Read the reasons if publishing is refused

features.name: Managing candidates and classes
features.description: Staff can add candidates individually or in bulk, search for them, and place them into classes or cohorts.
user_flows: Navigate to /candidates -> Add a candidate with a name and address -> Save the candidate -> Search for a candidate by part of a name -> Import candidates from CSV and review the preview -> Open a class -> Select members for the class -> Save the membership changes

features.name: Sending an exam to people
features.description: A coordinator chooses an exam and assigns it to a person or a class, then distributes secure links that can later be reissued or revoked.
user_flows: Navigate to /assignments -> Choose an exam -> Search for a person by name, address, or reference -> Or choose a class -> Set an expiry and the number of attempts -> Send the assignment -> Copy the returned link -> Reissue a lost link or revoke a leaked one

features.name: Watching and marking sittings
features.description: Staff can monitor active sittings, end a sitting early when needed, discard invalid sittings, and manually mark answers that require review.
user_flows: Navigate to /results/running -> Watch a sitting in progress and its remaining time -> End the sitting early and give a reason -> Discard a sitting that should never have started -> Open the review queue -> Mark a written answer -> Award marks and add feedback

features.name: Configuring the organisation
features.description: Administrators configure the organisation’s identity and defaults, including branding, support details, time zone, and result-release behavior.
user_flows: Navigate to /settings -> Set the organisation name -> Upload the organisation mark -> Choose a brand colour -> Enter a support address -> Set the time zone -> Save the settings

features.name: Host administration of organisations
features.description: A host administrator can search organisations, add a new organisation with its first administrator, and delete an organisation after confirmation.
user_flows: Navigate to /organisations -> Search the organisations on the deployment -> Add a new organisation -> Enter the organisation details and first administrator credentials -> Save the organisation -> Delete an organisation after typing its name to confirm

tech_stack: ABP Framework 10.6 client (@abp/ng.core) over a .NET 10 API
Bootstrap 5 utilities over a bespoke design-token layer
OpenIddict authorization code flow with PKCE
Arabic-first, right-to-left by default; English is the alternate

features.name: Sitting an exam from a link
features.description: A candidate opens the link they were emailed, reads what they are about to sit, starts it, answers under a server-held clock, and submits. There is no account and no password: the token is the entire credential, so nothing may require a sign-in anywhere on this path.
user_interactions: Open the exam link and read the exam title, duration and attempts left
Click "ابدأ الامتحان" / "Start the exam"
Answer a question with the control its type calls for
Move between questions using the question map
Watch the remaining time count down
Submit, and be warned first about questions left blank
Read the result, or the sentence saying it is withheld

features.name: Answering each of thirteen question types
features.description: Single choice, multi-select, true/false, free text, numeric, scale, ordering, matching, fill in the blank, code, hotspot, file upload and audio response. Each has its own control; the answer is saved as the candidate works.
user_interactions: Choose one option, or several
Type a written answer, or a number, or code
Drag or press to reorder items
Pair items across two columns
Point at a place on an image
Upload a file, or record audio

features.name: Signing in as staff
features.description: Coordinators, authors, markers and administrators sign in through the ABP account pages and return to the app.
user_interactions: Enter a username and a password
Return to the app signed in, seeing only what the role permits

features.name: Authoring an exam and its questions
features.description: Writing an exam, adding questions of any type, laying it out in sections, giving it a blueprint, and publishing it. Publishing is refused with every reason at once rather than one click at a time.
user_interactions: Create an exam with a title, a duration and a pass mark
Add questions, choosing a type and filling its own editor
Import questions from a CSV file
Add sections, and rules that draw from the shared bank
Publish, and read why publishing is refused

features.name: Sending an exam to people
features.description: A coordinator picks an exam and either a person or a whole class, and each recipient gets their own link. The link can be reissued, extended or revoked afterwards.
user_interactions: Choose an exam
Search for a person by name, address or reference
Or choose a class
Set an expiry and how many attempts
Send, and copy the link that comes back
Reissue a link somebody lost, or revoke one that leaked

features.name: Managing candidates and classes
features.description: Adding people one at a time or by CSV import, and putting them into classes. Searching is done on the server and matches a fragment of a name, an address or a reference — including Arabic written another way.
user_interactions: Add a person with a name and an address
Import a list from CSV and read the preview before committing
Search for somebody by part of their name
Open a class and tick people into it

features.name: Watching and marking sittings
features.description: Seeing which sittings are running, ending one that hung, discarding a test run, and marking the answers a machine cannot mark.
user_interactions: Watch a sitting in progress and its remaining time
End a sitting early, giving a reason
Discard a sitting that should never have started
Mark a written answer, award marks, and write feedback the candidate reads

features.name: Configuring the organisation
features.description: The name, mark, colour, support address, clock, default pass mark and whether results reach candidates directly. All of it is shown to candidates, so it is not decoration.
user_interactions: Set the organisation's name and upload its mark
Choose a brand colour
Give an address candidates can write to when something goes wrong
Set the time zone every exam clock is read in

features.name: Host administration of organisations
features.description: Adding an organisation with its first administrator, renaming it, and deleting it — which removes everything it owns.
user_interactions: Search the organisations on this deployment
Add one, with the address and password of its first administrator
Delete one, typing its name back to confirm

known_limitations.issue: A section's own clock, its minimum percentage and its "must be passed" flag are stored and read by nothing. Every candidate gets the exam's single clock, and no section can fail an exam on its own. The screen says so in words rather than hiding it.
known_limitations.impact: An author who relies on them gets a result that does not reflect the rule they thought they set.

known_limitations.issue: Code questions are marked by comparing the candidate's text with the expected output. Code is never executed.
known_limitations.impact: A correct program that prints something formatted differently is marked wrong. The authoring form says which of the two questions is being written.

known_limitations.issue: Until a sending domain is verified with the mail provider, invitations can only be delivered to the account holder's own address.
known_limitations.impact: On this deployment a real candidate would not receive their link, and the link is the only way into the exam.
